extra.reason: Fixed. A followed chain now answers the question the option asks in bytes: the engine keeps the wire truth (RedirectHop.RequestRaw/ResponseRaw, Response.Raw on the final response; hop requests rendered once so the scope gate authorises exactly the bytes the transport writes, hops sent via SendAs under the same rules as the operator's own send), the web layer maps them onto repeaterHop.request/response riding the send's own response, and the Repeater pane offers First/Final response plus per-hop 'View response' in the chain table — the chain is additive,  stays the operator's own. Follow-up fix the new tests caught: redirectRequest advertised the hop's Host as the bare hostname, dropping a non-default port — contradicts Burp's decompiled Zxrb.Zv authority rendering (host only for https/443 and http/80, host:port otherwise, IPv6 bracketed; :authority rewritten per hop on h2) and RFC 9112 3.2; hostPortFor now mirrors it. Evidence: sender tests TestAFollowedHopKeepsTheBytesItSentAndReceived / TestAnUnfollowedHopCarriesNoBytes / TestTheRawEntryKeepsTheFirstResponseBytesOnFinal, web test TestRepeaterServesTheChainHopsBytesAlongsideTheSend + byteless-refused-hop assertions; go build/vet/gofmt clean, whole-tree go test 38 pkgs ok, e2e-go.sh 24/0, e2e-ui 157 unit + axe green — e2e-ui's 8 failing specs fail identically at HEAD (bisected in a separate worktree) and are filed separately.

Fixed: all 8 failing specs resolved and the fixes verified manually in a real browser (agent-browser) as requested. Root causes: (1) RepeaterPage rendered hooks after its empty-state return — 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render' killed every fresh-browser flow (5 specs); hooks moved unconditional, a4dd7d5. (2) renderTabTrigger's ContextMenu wrapper had no key — React unkeyed-children console error the suite asserts against (1 spec); keyed on tab id, a4dd7d5. (3) dock-persistence spec used a '.editor' class that exists nowhere (editor root is editor-shell) — spec fix 0a41a14. (4) proxyGet was describe-scoped but called from another describe — ReferenceError; moved to module scope, 0a41a14. (5) in-scope-only spec asserted an empty-state string the product never rendered ('this filter' vs 'these filters') — spec fix, 0a41a14. (6) decoder spec clicked Add inside a collapsed empty section; now expands first, 0a41a14. Product fix discovered by manual testing: a typed history query matching nothing claimed 'No traffic captured yet' while a seeded capture sat behind it — the typed query was not in activeFilterNames; now named, verified live in the browser ('No exchange matches these filters ... query host = ...'), a4dd7d5. Note: full playwright suite was interrupted at 218/1 (decoder spec) before the expand-first spec fix; unit suites green throughout (go 38 pkgs, UI 157).

Forward all shipped: engine ForwardAll (mirrors DropAll once-only gate + single signal, forwards held bytes unmodified — nil would wake the client to an empty message), POST /api/intercept/forward-all answering the honest count, toolbar button between Forward and Drop all with the queue-moved toast, no confirmation needed for the safe direction. Verified manually in agent-browser: 3 held -> one click -> queue empty, clients unblocked with own bytes, history rows present. Engine test TestEngine_ForwardAllForwardsEveryHeldMessageUnmodifiedAndCountsOnlyItsOwn, web tests, route manifest, UI unit 157/0 green. Commits: see forward-all commit on ui-react-comparison.

Shipped in 7b29220: Pretty view is editable; every keystroke writes back through compactMessage (message.ts), which inverts the prettifier — JSON re-stringified minified, markup collapsed back to the inter-tag breaks prettyMarkup inserted, head kept byte-identical, mid-edit JSON parse failure passes the operator's text through unchanged. The wire bytes, Raw and Hex all agree with the compacted body, so the 'reformatted body is not the bytes sent' objection no longer applies. Tests: 6 new compactMessage contract tests in message.test.ts (Pretty edit round-trips to minified bytes; edited head preserved verbatim; mid-edit JSON pass-through; pure-tag markup round-trips byte-identically and is a prettyMessage fixed point; multi-line text-node newlines preserved; non-formattable body untouched). bun run check: 163 pass / 0 fail / 354 expect. Go gate clean.

The first explicit click, including a click back to Raw, wins for the pane's life via pickedRef — same deal Burp gives a pane once the operator has expressed a preference. A message whose Pretty view disappears falls back to Raw. bun run check: 163 pass / 0 fail.

POST /api/scope gained the 'toggle' action matching RemoveScoped's exact tuple identity; GET reports enabled on every row. scope_rules_v3 carries an enabled column (NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 via addColumn; every pre-column row was active), round-trip pinned by TestRestoreKeepsAScopeRulesDisabledState. Engine tests: TestDisablingAnIncludeRuleTakesItsHostsOutOfScope, TestDisablingAnExcludeRuleLetsItsHostsBackIn (with the include list admitting the host — exclude-wins semantics are not overridden by the toggle), TestMayContainHostSeesADisabledRuleTheSameWayContainsDoes, TestSetRuleEnabledMatchesTheTupleExactly. API tests: disable/re-enable loop, exclude direction, 404 on a nonexistent tuple. Scope page has the Enabled checkbox column wired to toggle. Verified live: toggle→enabled:false persists across a server restart and the Repeater send to that host is refused while disabled. Commit 85b0b63.

core.Scope gained dropOutOfScope (seed off), enforced at AuthoriseRequest and AuthoriseRaw — the two places a request is actually issued. AuthoriseRaw's refusal says 'dropped: ...' so egress is distinguishable from retention. Deliberately NOT wired into MayContainHost: filtering its include loop on Enabled returns default-allow when every include is disabled, the opposite of Contains — that would re-open the cj7x disagreement; the doc comment records why. GET /api/scope reports drop_out_of_scope; POST action drop_out_of_scope flips it (nil enabled refused 400). Persisted via settings key scope.drop_out_of_scope, restored in Store.Restore beside the rules. Scope page has Burp's 'Out-of-scope request handling' card with the checkbox. Tests: TestDropOutOfScope* (engine, incl. disabled-includes and excludes-win), TestAuthoriseRawNamesTheDrop/KeepsThePlainRefusal, TestMayContainHostIsUnchangedByTheDropSwitch, TestRestoreKeepsTheDropOutOfScopeSwitch (persist), TestTheDropOutOfScopeSwitchRoundTripsThroughTheAPI + refusal test (web). Verified live: proxied request to an unscoped host refused with the switch on; switch survives restart. Commit 2173be9.

WebSocket history frame list narrows by direction, opcode and payload substring — server-side on /api/ws/history (new direction/opcode/payload params; payload read through WsPayload per candidate because the bytes are not on the row; unknown direction/opcode refused 400 rather than ignored, matching the exchange param's rule). UI gains the toolbar (direction, opcode, debounced substring, clear-when-set) and the empty state distinguishes 'no frames match the filters' from 'no frames on this connection' from 'nothing captured yet'. Query key carries all three axes so cache entries cannot cross views. Bambda framing not reintroduced, per 8sa. Tests: TestWsHistoryFiltersByDirectionOpcodeAndPayload, TestWsHistoryRefusesUnknownFilterValues. Committed b4ad874.

useMessageLayout + MessageLayoutSwitch in ui/layout.tsx: horizontal / vertical / combined, persisted per surface under burpsy.layout.<storageId> (same localStorage contract as SplitPane's divider), defaulting to each surface's prior hardcoded orientation. History (highest-frequency surface) wired first: the annotate bar carries the three-icon radiogroup; combined renders the pair as Request/Response Tabs with one mounted editor and the grid collapses to one track so the Inspector keeps its column. Verified live against the running binary: horizontal side-by-side with Inspector, combined single-pane tabs, vertical default, choice survives reload (pressed icon + grid class restored). Remaining pages take the same hook with no new design. Commit a11f255.

SequencerReport gained extra_stats (chi_square, serial_correlation + caveat label, monte_carlo_pi/deviation, repeated_tokens + repeated_list) computed by extraFor() sharing the engine's own ChiSquare/SerialCorrelation/MonteCarloPi/DetectPatterns — the two front-ends now read one set of numbers. Serial correlation is labelled in the JSON itself as 'not Burp's bit-position correlation test' so the conflation the issue warns about cannot happen silently. The Sequencer page gains the 'Uniformity & duplicates' card; repeated tokens lead and go warn-toned when non-zero. Tests: TestReportCarriesTheDuplicateTokenCount, TestReportShowsZeroDuplicatesForDistinctTokens, TestReportCarriesChiSquareAndItRisesWithSkew (uniform → exactly 0 per expected=total/distinct semantics, skewed → larger), TestSerialCorrelationLabelNamesTheCaveat, TestReportCarriesMonteCarloPi. Verified live: POST /api/sequencer/analyse returns extra_stats with the duplicate named; card renders. Commit 1da4916.

POST /api/sequencer/capture/pause and /resume hold the newest live capture between sends (never inside one — the in-flight send records whole). The wire's paused flag is the loop's own pausedAtGate, not the handler's request: the one send already on the wire when pause lands still records, and a sample growing 'while paused' is the lie the flag-split avoids (found by the test racing it). 409 when nothing runs or the capture finished; GET refused like stop. Copy tokens / Save tokens ride the view's existing token list (no new route); UI gains Pause/Resume (Play/Pause icons) and both export buttons, guarded on an empty sample. Tests: TestACaptureCanBePausedAndResumedWithoutLosingTokens (freeze + no loss + resume growth), TestPausingWithNoLiveCaptureIsRefused, TestCaptureViewCarriesTheTokensForExport (non-empty, no blank tokens). Verified live: 12→12 frozen across 1s, 12→21 after resume, paused flag accurate. Commit 2237cfd.

Issues filter bar rebuilt as Burp's combinable checkbox groups: 'Show only' severity (5) and confidence (3) over Set<string> — empty set means no constraint, non-empty is an allow-list, so High+Medium shows together. Hide-false-positive checkbox rides the existing false_positive wire flag (no backend change; the tree already dims FPs). Empty state counts any active filter. Verified live with seeded findings: High alone 1, +Medium 5, +hide-FP 4, cleared 5; FP row dimmed throughout. Commit d11fcce. (hide-duplicate not built: findings already merge into one row with occurrences — there is no duplicate row to hide; the merge IS the dedup.)

POST /api/issues/record creates a hand-recorded finding attached to one exchange: first-class (same store/triage/persistence), confidence defaults Certain (operator saw it — stronger than any scanner), severity defaults Low (ungraded must not inflate High), exchange_id is *uint64 because exchange 0 is real (dense counters from zero). Same-name+host records merge via ordinary dedup — Burp's 'adds to a previously created issue'. Comment rides the Triage path (operator state, one write path). UI: 'Record an issue' in Engagement tools of the shared row/editor menu, three prompts, issues list invalidated. Route pinned riskLocal in the manifest. Tests: TestAnIssueCanBeRecordedByHandAgainstAnExchange, TestARecordedIssueDefaults*, TestARecordedIssueWithoutADescriptionNamesItsExchange, TestARecordedIssueCarriesTheOperatorsComment, TestRecordingAgainstAMissingExchangeIsRefused, TestASecondRecordWithTheSameNameMergesIntoTheFirst. Verified live: curl record (id 10, Medium/Certain, exchange 4) and UI context-menu record ('Issue #11 recorded against #4'). Commit b3d6b63.

Organizer filter gains the three missing axes: search term over title/note/host/path/method with Regex, Case-sensitive and Negative checkboxes (uncompileable regex matches nothing, not everything — a broken filter must not silently pass), file-extension filter (last dot-segment of the response path, options offered only for extensions present), and Annotated-only (note non-empty or highlight set beyond the picker's 'none' value, whose string length would otherwise count as an annotation). Unresolved rows stay exempt per the page's existing contract. Verified live: 'metadata' 2/14, ^Users 2, negative jwt 12, annotated 4, pdf 7, png 3, clear 14; 'showing N of 14' counter tracks. Commit b9be50c.

Held messages carry the operator's comment and highlight: intercept.Held.Comment/Highlight + SetAnnotation (unknown ids error), heldView reports both, POST /api/intercept/annotate/{id} writes them (first segment 'annotate' cannot be an id — no collision with /{id}/forward|drop; manifest entry added). Proxy request-hold path copies the annotation off the resolved hold into the recorded exchange's note/highlight — Burp's 'annotations that you make also appear against the item in HTTP history' — pinned by TestAHeldAnnotationsRideForwardIntoHistory. Unrecorded (dont_log_out_of_scope) traffic drops it with the exchange; WS holds pass explicit empties. Intercept page gains the annotation bar under the editor (comment input + colour select + Save, disabled while unchanged; empty highlight clears). Repaired the orphaned half found in-tree: ws.go updated to the new completeResponse signature, annotate tests arm the request list (enable alone does not hold). Verified live: annotated held #1 through the UI (comment+red) and the queue view reports both fields. Commit b862a76.

sender.ProtocolPreferenceForceH2: force means the request rides h2 when carriable at all (same construct bar as Auto) — a request h2 cannot carry still goes out as HTTP/1.1 verbatim with the construct named (force must not re-encode), and a target whose ALPN declines h2 reports DowngradeNegotiatedHTTP11 rather than failing the handshake (an h2-only offer would abort at exactly the h2-downgrade target being probed). Wire: protocol_preference "http2" in the allowlist + mapping; Repeater select gains Force HTTP/2. The documented deliberate absence (an ALPN override) is untouched — that is a switch no raw-byte send could honour; a protocol preference is a different control. Tests: TestForceH2SendsOverHTTP2WhenTheRequestIsCarriable (h2 despite the cache having learnt http/1.1), TestForceH2AtAnHTTP11TargetDowngradesAndNamesIt, TestForceH2CannotCarryAnUnrepresentableRequest (framing headers verbatim on the wire). Commit 5c6993e.

GET/POST /api/intercept/startup with Burp's three modes (on / off / restore); restore reuses the live state the enable endpoint records on every toggle; absent reads off (a preference nobody wrote must not turn interception on); unknown mode 400; applied through WithPersist's restore path; 503 when no persistence is attached (the preference would not survive). Settings page gains the 'Default Proxy interception state' select. Tests: TestInterceptStartupModeRoundTrips (round-trip, fresh default off, unknown refused) and TestRestoreStartupBringsBackTheLastLiveState (enable live, restart over the same DB, switch comes back on). Commits ae4ab2b (backend) + 2f99ae5 (UI).

Store gains editorFont (12/13/14/16/18px, default 12px = the old hardcoded value) and uiScale (100/110/125/150%), persisted with theme/density in burpsy.workspace. app.tsx applies --editor-font-size and --ui-scale on <html> beside data-theme; editor.tsx's theme reads var(--editor-font-size) instead of the literal (gutters calc(size-1px) preserving the 12/11 relationship); the fluid type tokens re-derive as calc(clamp(...) * var(--ui-scale)) so the chrome scales while the editor — on its own variable — does not. Appearance gains the two selects under Table density. Verified live: 150%/16px updates both custom properties, persists, survives reload, fresh Repeater editor computes 16px. Commit a1b7bf5.

Two new proxy options in the Miscellaneous family, both wired live through ApplyRequestEgress on both relay paths (after M&R and intercept, so operator rules/edits see the client's real bytes): strip_proxy_headers (whole Proxy- prefix family; seeded ON — the engine never forwarded one; the switch sends them for origins being tested for their own handling) and set_connection_close (request header rewritten, response header set, TLS loop stops after one exchange so neither peer waits). Settings page Transport adjustments card gains both switches. The every-option binding test gained the requestEgressFixture (no per-key table), and TestProxyHeaderFamilyIsStrippedByDefault / TestProxyHeadersPassWhenTheSwitchIsOff prove the seed both directions through a live proxy loop; TestConnectionCloseRewritesBothSides asserts the response header and that a second request on the socket is not served. Remaining members of Burp's Miscellaneous panel are the three separately-filed behavioural gaps (6rb, pi8, am6) plus HTTP/1.0-forcing, which this engine cannot represent (it speaks HTTP/1.1 on egress); noted rather than shipped as a decorative switch. Commit 976c899.

intruder.URLEncodeSet(ps, chars): the final pass — named characters percent-encoded per UTF-8 byte, everything else untouched (the whole-payload encode rule remains the separate tool); spaces and control characters always encoded additionally (a payload containing them cannot be delivered); empty named set with nothing unrepresentable is the off state. Applied in handleIntruderRun AFTER the operator's rule chain (Burp's placement) — the two compose. Wire: url_encode_characters on /api/intruder/run. UI: the box under Payload processing, seeded with Burp's default list, clearable to disable. Tests: TestURLEncodeSet* (5, incl. multi-byte per-byte and the always-encode rule), TestIntruderRunAppliesURLEncodeCharacters (wire, x y -> x%20y in the echo). Commits d93be4f + 2847ca9.

Interaction table triage: protocol filter derived from the rows (covers dns/http/smtp/ldap — one more than Burp's three buttons), search over interaction_id/type/q_type/client_ip/payload plus the annotation, per-row mark-as-read + mark-all-read, per-interaction comment/highlight (inline annotate row: comment input + colour select), hide-read toggle, and an unread/all-read badge in the section heading. Read state and annotations persist in the workspace store (per-browser view state, like the Inspector dock — the channel is a subprocess-appended log nothing here owns); the unread count on the tool tab itself rides burpsy-react-ui-xvo's tab-attention work, with the in-page badge carrying it meanwhile. Verified live with real callbacks: minted a payload, resolved it so the public pool logged 3 DNS interactions; filter dns=3/http=0, search AAAA=2 / by comment=1, mark-read flips badge to 'all read', annotation survives reload. Commit 0d3ba46.

Suite-wide pause/resume: dash.Registry gains a paused atomic gate + GateCheck(ctx) (50ms tick, cancellation senior — pause+cancel stops cleanly); tasks already inside one unit finish it, which is the contract, not a limitation. POST /api/tasks/pause|resume with {paused, running} — the running count is the honest part of the reply on an empty dashboard. Sequencer capture takes the gate at its existing between-sends placement. Dashboard: 'Pause all tasks' / 'Resume tasks' button + 'Task execution is paused' warning bar; paused rides the dashboard poll (dashboardResp.Paused). Tests: TestTheSuiteWidePauseRoundTripsThroughTheAPI (gate is state, survives a task finishing, idempotent), TestPausingWithNothingRunningReportsZero, TestGateCheckYieldsToCancellation. Verified live: pause flips button + warning bar + toast 'Tasks paused (0 running)', API reads paused:true; resume clears all. Commits caaca7f (backend), 2868d3b (UI).

/api/report/{json,sarif,html} accept severity (comma list, strict — unknown value 400 rather than silently informational, since a typo would produce an only-informational report claiming to be the filtered set), host (substring over the finding's resolved hosts), and exclude_false_positives=true. All three compose; zero-value filter = the whole store, so the unparameterised URL means what it always did. One reportRows(filter) feeds all three formats so they cannot disagree. Tests: TestTheUnfilteredReportCarriesEverything, TestTheReportFiltersBySeverity, ...ByHostSubstring, ...CanExcludeFalsePositives, ...FiltersCompose, ...RefusesAnUnknownSeverity. Commit 2e47dac.

AutoPause predicate over the same bytes Grep.run reads, firing Control.Pause — the mechanism existed; this is the trigger. Appears mode = any expression matches; missing mode = none does (complement over ONE list). Simple strings quote-meta + case-fold unless case_sensitive; regex compiled as given; uncompilable expression refused 400 at the run endpoint (an auto-pause that silently never fires lies by omission). In-flight response collected whole; pause holds future enumerations (the same in-flight-window rule Control documents; fixtures run 1-wide to make the hold observable). Report carries auto_paused (attack-level atomic so ReArm-on-resume cannot erase the account of who pressed the button). Wire: intruderRunReq.auto_pause {expressions, missing, simple, case_sensitive}. Tests: appears halts (no NEW sends while paused — asserted on the sender counter, settled counts race by design), missing halts, case-sensitivity, regex-as-given, uncompilable refused, nil inert, wire round-trip auto_paused non-zero. Commit 0554b6d.

Live capture becomes a worker pool: threads (default 1 = the historical sequential capture, cap 32, refused beyond rather than clamped). Claims CAS-issued from an atomic counter — claims are promises to send, attempts are settled sends; the sequential loop's attempt()<requested check was safe only because one goroutine ran it. Both pauses gate between sends in every worker (same placement as before, so a pause never splits a response). Miss-streak guard: per-worker streak, so a location that never matches stops in the same order of magnitude of requests the sequential guard produced (a global streak ÷ thread count would have cost threads×25 requests on a broken location). Cancellation classifies in the closer — several workers see ctx.Done at once and exactly one task.Stop lands, so the dashboard reads a cancelled capture as stopped. Wire: threads on the capture request; form gains the field with the shared-bound caveat in the hint. Tests: threads=1 never overlaps, threads=4 overlaps and collects every token, threads=33 refused, wide pool never claims one ordinal twice (origin stamps tokens at ACCEPT time — stamping at write time races across overlapping connections and mimics the duplicate-claim defect). Verified live through the UI: three 100-token captures completed. Commit c36ce21.

transforms.ts gains the full Burp variant set: URL all-chars, URL all-chars %uXXXX Unicode, HTML numeric entities (all chars), HTML hex entities (all chars), Base64-URL encode/decode, and Construct string per dialect (JS double/single, SQL Microsoft/Oracle/MySQL — 'admin'+'CHAR(39)' quoting differs per dialect, which is why one generic escape was never the answer). Editor Convert selection group carries all of them beside the existing six, same editable-in-place/read-only-dialog contract. 13 transform tests pin the primitives. Verified live through the menu: 'a=b&c d' -> %61%3D%62%26%63%20%64; admin'-- -> 'admin'+CHAR(39)+'--'; Base64-URL round trip; %u003C%u0062%u003E for <b>. Commits d97af46 + dist.

SessionRule.ScopeParams + MatchParams (every named parameter present, case-insensitive — csrf_token vs CSRF_Token is the same parameter; empty = unrestricted, matching MatchHost's empty-list contract so legacy rules cannot silently stop matching). MatchingRuleFor(host, params) is the evaluating entry point; MatchingRule stays parameter-less so callers that could pass params but don't are visible in grep. Login probe passes its steps' parameter names (URL query + form-urlencoded body — Burp's two scope surfaces; JSON has no names without a schema). Axis is a restriction, not a priority: scoped-first claims its requests and falls through everything else. Persisted as session_rules.scope_params (JSON list, DEFAULT '' via addColumn — legacy reads unrestricted, the only safe default). UI: scope_params on the rule DTO both directions (omitted=everywhere), editor gains the parameter list mirroring the host list, summary reads 'every host carrying csrf_token'. Tests: unrestricted/any, match/miss, conjunction, case-insensitive, coordinator order semantics both orders, legacy-persist unrestricted + scoped conjunction survival, wire create/list round-trip. Verified live: rule created through the running UI with scope_params=[csrf_token]. Commit abb9bd8.

ValidityRule gains regex + case_sensitive (applied to body_contains / body_not_contains / url_contains; regexes case-fold like literals until CaseSensitive or the pattern's own inline flag — (?s) preserved, no double-(?i) rewriting) and url_contains (the redirection target the macro runner RESOLVES — Location against the step URL, never followed: reading is not sending). No-redirect = Indeterminate clause with All{} precedence (definite Invalid outranks, Valid softens). Evaluate carries finalURL through All/Any/Not; 9 production call sites updated, HandleResponse passes '' explicitly (live traffic follows no chain). ValidateValidityPatterns refuses uncompilable regexes with a 400 naming the pattern at save (no-match-forever is a control that lies by omission). UI: two checkboxes + target field on the validity card; validity is free-form JSON so no DTO change. Tests: TestLiteralBodyMatchingIsCaseFoldedByDefault, TestRegexDialMakesBodyContainsAPattern, TestAnUncompilableRegexReportsNoMatch, TestBodyNotContainsHonoursTheDials, TestURLContainsMatchesTheRedirectTarget, TestURLContainsWithNoRedirectIsIndeterminate, TestURLClauseComposesThroughAllAnyNot. Verified live: UI-saved rule carries {status_is, regex:true, url_contains:'/dashboard'}. Commit 2016405.

TLS passthrough section (previously Settings-only, the cause of FALSE finding burpsy-react-ui-wyp) now renders in the Proxy settings leaf between the response-modification switches and outcome counters — where Burp files it (configPanelProxyTlsPassThrough, TOOLS_PROXY_OPTIONS anchor in BurpClass9055). The section is an exported shared component (single source, no duplicate editing surface); the Settings page no longer carries its own copy. Verified live: Proxy settings shows the card with Add rule; Settings has no own TLS passthrough heading. Commit f3de24d.

Both result tables have a right-click menu: Send to Repeater, request or response into either Comparer slot, Copy request, each greyed when the bytes were not stored. Engine gained RecordRequest/RequestFn so a row can name its exact spliced request (bounded: 500 detail rows + 2000 bucket exemplars, one Put when they coincide; MCP/CLI callers unchanged). Live-verified end to end in Chromium by specs/intruder-handoff.spec.ts, which reads the delivered bytes back out of the Repeater editor. f439a6f

collector.errors, PayloadSet.Dropped and BucketExample.Payloads were nil slices marshalling to JSON null against a TS type that declares them non-nullable arrays; every zero-failure attack took the Results tab down with the ErrorBoundary. All three now start empty at their single construction sites. Pinned by two tests that assert the marshalled JSON (Go cannot tell nil from empty) — both fail if the initialisers are removed. f439a6f

Repeater menu gains 'Paste host / URL as request'. Completed another agent's half-done work: requestFromUrl existed in lib/api.ts but was called by nothing and had no tests. Wiring it up found two defects — the pasted scheme went straight into 'target', so ws:// and wss:// built tabs that 400 on first Send (targetParts knows only http/https), and an unknown scheme (ftp:, file:) did the same instead of refusing. Both fixed. 7 unit tests + 2 browser specs that read the built request back out of the rendered tab. 01e4f30

AuthoriseRequest now consults the switch instead of returning a bare Contains, and both proxy relay paths ask it before forwarding — ahead of the dont_log_out_of_scope branch, which forwards. Refusal is 403 with Scope.Explain naming the deciding rule, on the decrypted channel for TLS. Five tests assert whether the ORIGIN was contacted, not what the client was told; each half of the fix is pinned by a failing-without-it test. 3702b57

taskAction now requires POST on pause, resume and {id}/cancel (405 + Allow). Also generalised the route-manifest 405 sweep: specs gain actionPaths, a sub-path->allowed-verb map swept with its own method set, so a subtree routing /api/tasks/1 to DELETE and /api/tasks/1/cancel to POST has both covered — the single-subPath design is what let the original narrowing hide the gap. Pinned: removing the guard fails the sweep. bb089f0

findingToIssueView initialises v.Occurrences to an empty slice, so a finding with no resolvable occurrence goes out as [] not null. Third instance of the nil-slice/null class after 9pxd; test asserts the marshalled JSON because Go cannot tell nil from empty. bb089f0

URLEncodeSet decodes per-rune (the named set is characters, so multi-byte must match as a unit) but writes from the input byte slice, and a byte that is not valid UTF-8 passes through as itself — it is in no named set and no safe set, which is the function's own documented rule. Empty-set fast path is now a byte scan too. Table test pins the boundary incl. four invalid-byte shapes; positive control fails with 61 ef bf bd 62. f7c6db8

reportRows and reportFilter.applies both use EffectiveSeverity/EffectiveConfidence, matching findingToIssueView. Four assertions, all failing without the fix: the exported value in both fields, and the filter in both directions (?severity=critical must find the raised finding, ?severity=low must not). Test triages through the real Triage path rather than constructing an already-overridden finding.

CheckContext gains InsertionKinds (from the scanner's effective AuditConfig) and ProbeInsertionKinds(); all 15 probe sites across 5 checks_*.go files now ask it instead of naming DefaultProbeInsertionKinds. 'none' survives to the probe so a run configured to insert nowhere probes nowhere; an unconfigured run keeps the default unchanged. Guarded by a source check that fails if any check site names the literal again — reproduced. 21f26e2

Exported csvCell from api.ts and routed intruder-export.ts's intruderReportToCSV through it, removing the unguarded local copy. Added two csv-guard.test.ts cases (= and @ leading payload text); verified they fail against the reverted unguarded implementation (both toContain assertions failed, showing the raw unguarded cell) and pass with the fix restored. Gate green: tsc --noEmit, bun test (all files), bun run build (only dist/app.js diffed), go build ./....

The two rules' prefix is now tagPrefix — (?:[^>"']|"[^"]*"|'[^']*')*? — which consumes either a non-quote character or an ENTIRE quoted run, so it cannot stop part-way through a value. RE2 has no lookbehind, so this is structural rather than asserted. 12-case table: five corruption shapes, two already-safe ones kept as regressions, four real attributes still deleted, and one real attribute BEYOND a value that mentions the word (which a fix that simply refused to cross a quote would fail). Positive control reproduces all three original corruptions. 8c9dbb4

Fixed: the border used var(--accent-<colour>), a token styles.css never defines (only --accent/-bright/-strong/-contrast exist); every colour fell to the same fallback. Switched to var(--highlight-<colour>), the token History/Organizer's row-highlight-* rules already bind to distinct hex values, and replaced the picker's invented/partial option list with the shared HIGHLIGHTS vocabulary. Extracted highlightBorderStyle as a pure function (repo has no DOM test harness) and added collaborator.test.ts, which cross-checks the emitted var() name against the real styles.css rather than just string-diffing two outputs. Verified it fails against the original --accent-<colour> code (2/3 tests failed, naming the undefined token) and passes with the fix (3/3). Did not add a live e2e spec — real Collaborator rows need a reachable interaction server, disproportionate for a P3 token fix. Gate green (tsc, targeted bun test, build only touching dist/app.js, go build).

Crawler, ActiveScanner and intruder.Attack each gained an optional suiteGate func(context.Context), called between units of work, wired to s.tasks.GateCheck at four web call sites. Plain func not *dash.Registry (crawler does not import dash; an engine asking the task registry whether to keep working is the wrong dependency direction). Nil keeps CLI/MCP/tests unchanged. Five tests: the crawl asks the gate at least once per fetch (not once at the start), a held gate stops both the crawl and the attack, release resumes and loses no work. Both pinned by removing the call. 60370d9

Race: the sender callback's append is now mutex-guarded and copies the bytes (Run's default limits allow several in flight; engine_test.go's recordingSender already did this). Its positional sent[i] assertion became a set membership check — arrival order is not plan order under concurrency and the engine never promised it was. Flake: the fixture decremented inFlight AFTER writing the response, so the client could read, reconnect and be accepted before the decrement ran; it now decrements before the write, which the client cannot race. 30 consecutive runs clean; the threads=4 overlap assertion still passes 10/10, so the fix does not mask real detection. 4956fb2

Fixed: messageView now dechunks and decompresses before taking body_base64, via a plain variable updated at each unwrap step and a deferred Body64 assignment. Verified the fix-pinning tests fail without it (stashed api_types.go, reran, restored) with output showing the returned bytes did not match the original image. Added 2 new tests (chunked+gzip, chunked-only) plus 1 regression guard (DecodeError must stay empty for bad chunk framing on an uncompressed body). Full gate (build, vet excl. intruder, gofmt, go test ./... -timeout 30m) green. Committed as 6e62474.

ApplyRequestEgress moved below the intercept hold on both relay paths, into the same after-intercept slot the WebSocket strip and applyRequestRules already occupy. The store runs after that line, so recorded bytes and forwarded bytes stay identical; what changes is that the held request now shows the client's real headers. Test asserts both halves — the operator sees Proxy-Authorization, the origin does not — so a fix that simply stopped stripping would fail it. Positive control reproduces 'the held request had already been stripped'.

Fixed: added sendPlan.mustH2 (set from ProtocolPreferenceForceH2 at both carriable branches of planSend, false wherever h2 was never offered), so Auto and Force plans are no longer reflect.DeepEqual-identical. Consumed it (not a dead field): SendRawOutcome sets a new Downgrade.Forced bool from plan.mustH2 at the negotiated-http/1.1 branch. Consulted advisor first, since the bd body's 'Auto downgrades silently' claim is false of the current code (file header + protocol_test.go already require every HTTP/1.1 send, Auto included, to report a Downgrade) and force_h2_test.go already forbids Force erroring on ALPN decline -- so the only consistent shape was an additive observability bit, not a behavior change to the decline path. Verified failing without the fix: reverted sender.go/protocol.go via stash, new test file failed to compile (mustH2/Forced undefined), restored and confirmed pass. All 3 pre-existing force_h2_test.go tests pass unmodified. Full internal/sender suite + build/vet(excl. intruder)/gofmt green. Committed as ac31dc8.

Fixed: Comment and Highlight in toolLogSetComment's request struct changed from string to *string, matching the sibling toolLogSetCaptureReq.Filter/.Capacity pattern already in the same file. Each SetComment/SetHighlight call is now gated on its own field being present, so an absent JSON key leaves that axis untouched. Added an existence check via toolLog.All() for the empty-body edge case (neither field given), since SetComment/SetHighlight fold their own existence check into a mutation and there's no bare lookup. Verified failing without the fix (stashed api_toolkit.go, reran, restored) with output showing the highlight/comment getting cleared exactly as described. New test TestToolLogPatchLeavesTheOmittedAxisAlone covers comment-only, highlight-only, empty-on-known-id, and empty-on-unknown-id. Both pre-existing PATCH tests pass unmodified. Full gate (build, vet excl. intruder, gofmt, go test ./... -timeout 30m) green.

Added a Text/Hex toggle to Comparer (mirroring Decoder's Braces/Hash toggle) backed by buildHexRows, which builds each side's hex+ASCII grid from the diff ops and that side's own real encoded bytes rather than the text pane's GAP_CHAR-padded strings, so a whitespace-only or non-printable-byte difference reads as a real distinct hex byte instead of nothing or the padding glyph. Hunk numbering matches buildSegments exactly, so hunk highlighting and jump-to-hunk work in hex mode. Capped at 8192 bytes/side, mirroring Decoder's hexDump cap. Unit-tested (comparer.test.ts) with a proven-fails-without-fix case (side-selection regression: 1/4 failed with 'Expected: 3, Received: 2' before restoring the fix, 4/4 after). E2E-verified with a new spec (e2e/specs/comparer-hex.spec.ts) against a real rebuilt burpsy: confirmed it fails (times out waiting for the Hex button) against the true pre-fix source, and passes against the fix. Scoped regression checks on the built fix: routes.spec.ts --grep comparer (1/1 pass), a11y.spec.ts --grep '#comparer' both themes (2/2 pass, 0 violations). Did not run the full e2e-ui.sh suite per coordinator guidance — it carries four pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (smsz, 92o5, q4i0), all reproduced against HEAD. Gate green: tsc --noEmit, targeted bun test, build (only dist/app.js diffed), go build ./...

Fixed: handleProxyListener's PUT branch now checks errors.Is(err, syscall.EADDRINUSE) on Rebind's error (which proxy.Server.Rebind wraps with %w, so this sees through to the syscall errno without touching internal/proxy) and answers 409 for an occupied port, 400 for everything else. Corrected the existing test that encoded the bug (renamed to TestProxyListenerPutToAnOccupiedPortAnswers409AndKeepsTheOldListener, now asserts 409) and added TestProxyListenerPutToAnUnassignableAddressStays400 (binds 10.255.255.1, a valid IPv4 literal that fails fast with EADDRNOTAVAIL, not EADDRINUSE) to pin the distinction goes both ways. Verified failing without the fix (stashed api_proxylistener.go, reran, restored) with output showing 400 where 409 was wanted. Added a bd comment on -77m correcting its aspirational 409/400 claim. Full gate (build, vet excl. intruder, gofmt, go test ./... -timeout 30m) green.

core.Exchange and scanner.CapturedExchange gain ServerIP, read off the live upstream socket at all five proxy capture sites via serverIPOf; forwardRequest returns it with the response since it owns and closes the socket. Wire field is unconditional so '' (nobody recorded it) is distinguishable from an older server. History gains the IP column. Integration test asserts the exact loopback address through a real proxy. ee9e8c8

core.Exchange and scanner.CapturedExchange gain ListenerPort, taken from the CLIENT connection's local address (not the configured bind, which a rebind makes a different port from the one the request arrived on). Zero means 'not from a listener' — Repeater, Intruder, crawler, scanner — and renders as em-dash, not 0. Test asserts the port equals the test's own listener and NOT the origin's, which is what reading the wrong socket end would fail. ee9e8c8
